newsitem.title: UK: LME copper rises, cash/threes in contango briefly.
newsitem.headline: LME copper rises, cash/threes in contango briefly.

text.p: Copper prices ended an uncertain LME session with modest gains on Tuesday as an easing trend in nearby spreads was partially reversed in the afternoon.

Copper's cash/three months spread momentarily traded at a $2 contango - the first time the benchmark spread has been in contango since January 1995. At its peak in December 1995 the backwardation was some $330.

But spread premiums have been under pressure for some time, and this was exacerbated after Monday's "third Wednesday" September pricing when previously tight dates fell out of the market's price structure.
The market is long of the nearby dates through to October, with a $5 contango prevailing, which offset temporarily the backwardations at the rear of the spread.
The cash/threes contango proved to be shortlived, as conditions were thin and some of the intermediate dates moved back into backwardation.
However, cash/threes was only showing a $2 backwardation at the close, against Monday's $8/9.
Forward business was mostly routine, with prices climbing off the lows as a 1,475-tonne decline in stocks was expected to be followed by further drawdowns.
But the going became sticky overhead and last business was at $1,870, up just $5 a tonne from Monday's kerb.
Aluminium notched up another two-year low, but the nadir of $1,411 induced some light trade buying and short-covering which temporarily halted the general decline of the last week.
But with stocks up 7,400 tonnes and expected to continue rising in the short-term the market is projected testing $1,400. Last business today was at $1,416.50, a $1.50 gain from Monday.
Nickel rose from the low in the afternoon, but was depressed after Monday's technical sell-off. LME stocks rose 510 tonnes while the Inco dispute is not a supportive factor at present.
Levels below $7,400 attracted some bargain-hunting buying, however, and the market closed at a steadier $7,430/40 a tonne.
Lead attempted a mini-rally this afternoon, with the market oversold, although the recovery was not enough to lift prices back into the plus column, traders said.
Charts are bearish under $800 and there is the possibility of further fund sales. By the kerb prices were retreating once more and last trade was at $772, a $13 loss from yesterday.

Zinc again encountered reasonable trade support on the dip below $1,020, which helped the market move higher in slow conditions. Last three months business was at $1,025, up $7 from the previous kerb.

Tin came under late pressure, diving below $6,100 when sell-stops were triggered and not helped by the general trend and a 85-tonne inventory increase. Last business was at $6,070, down $45 from yesterday.
Alloy was lower in customary slack conditions, with three months finishing at $1,230/35, against a previous $1,235/40.
